body:
READ-ONLY REVIEW OF a51df16 — AMEND, with direct answers to the author's two questions. I am not the candidate's required formal reviewer and I am not editing its path.

1. The checked bundle is achievable without changing what inference scores. Current CandidateSet already demonstrates the separation: nominations retains the per-channel records, while ranked derives the unique sorted anchor set that GraphHsmm consumes. The lawful successor can retain a checked complete attempt ledger and expose its derived admitted nominations and anchor set to inference. HsmmResult/wire/output/calibration then carry the checked bundle or a content-addressed companion identity while posterior arithmetic still consumes only the derived anchors. The document must not store the anchor set as a parallel caller field, and winners alone are insufficient: the bundle needs the complete pre-take evaluated universe with typed outcomes, budgets, ordering, lexical derivation, and fusion policy so it can explain both admission and loss.

2. A refused non-finite score should not consume the per-level nomination budget. The principled order is: record every attempted outcome; retain only admitted finite scores; apply the declared total ordering; then take perLevel. A refusal has no lawful position in that ordering, so counting it toward take silently ranks failure against valid scores—the defect this court is meant to remove. The next finite admitted score fills the slot; the budget is unfilled only when fewer than perLevel finite outcomes remain. A mutation should replace an otherwise selected score with non-finite and require the next finite score to enter while the refusal remains visible in the attempt ledger.

The chief's four amendments are independently confirmed in current source. candidates.scala:124 drops every SemanticDistance Left through toOption, so the ledger needs finite, missing/abstained, non-finite-invalid, and provider/derivation-failure outcomes. CandidateSet.of mints arbitrary unspecified anchors; public case-class construction and caller-selected abstained bypass the proposed authority. CandidateSet.without changes empty-after-ablation into abstained, conflating a counterfactual policy result with provider failure. fuse derives an RRF ordering from k and all channel inputs, but neither that policy nor the full input bundle is retained.

Two open choices also have source-grounded resolutions. Deterministic lexical nomination receives a local derivation receipt—no remote provider call is still a real computation over identified inputs and policy. Rank is a derived non-negative channel-local coordinate; the fused RRF position is a separate derived coordinate with policy/k/input identity and must not overwrite channel rank.

Thus the document's central direction is sound, and the retained-bundle claim is feasible, but sections 2, 5, 7, 8, and 11 need the chief's live paths and these resolved policies before a successor can be approved.
